item.text:
**Bottom line**
Putin’s 2024 crisis response was mostly coercive. The one clear positive was immediate tightening after the Crocus attack, but the broader pattern was external blame, collective punishment of migrants, punitive control of dissent, and a security state that was better at repression than civilian protection.

**Weak evidence for protection/restraint**

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [Shooting and blast reported at concert hall near Moscow -- agencies](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/shooting-and-blast-reported-at-concert-hall-near-moscow--agencies-3350167) | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-03-22 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/shooting-and-blast-reported-at-concert-hall-near-moscow--agencies-3350167 | After the Crocus attack, Russia tightened security at airports, transport hubs, and across Moscow and cancelled large public events. That is genuine crisis containment, but it was reactive and short-term rather than evidence of a broader restraint-oriented crisis doctrine. | `3B.9` |
| [Putin vows punishment for all those responsible for concert attack](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/putin-vows-punishment-for-all-those-responsible-for-concert-attack-3350557) | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-03-23 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/putin-vows-punishment-for-all-those-responsible-for-concert-attack-3350557 | Putin publicly promised punishment for the Crocus attackers and labeled the assault “international terrorism.” This is a suppressive response to violence, but it was paired with blame-shifting rather than a calm, rights-respecting security posture. | `3B.9`, also `3B.3` |

**Strong evidence against restraint**

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [Moscow shooting poses awkward questions for Russia's intelligence agencies](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/moscow-shooting-poses-awkward-questions-for-russias-intelligence-agencies-3352104) | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-03-25 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/moscow-shooting-poses-awkward-questions-for-russias-intelligence-agencies-3352104 | Reuters said Russia’s security state was effective at detaining Putin’s opponents but failed to stop the mass shooting. That suggests the apparatus was optimized for repression rather than for protecting the public during a domestic crisis. | `3B.9`, also `3B.2`, `3B.4` |
| [Russia 'Punishes' Tajik Migrants With Entry Denials, Deportations After Terror Attack](https://www.rferl.org/a/russia-punishes-tajik-migrants-deportations-entry-moscow-terror-attack/32891458.html) | RFE/RL | 2024-04-04 | https://www.rferl.org/a/russia-punishes-tajik-migrants-deportations-entry-moscow-terror-attack/32891458.html | Police raids, entry denials, deportations, and aggressive questioning of Tajik migrants after Crocus looked like collective punishment and intimidation of a vulnerable group, not restrained crisis management. | `3B.9`, also `3B.2`, `3B.3`, `3B.7` |
| [More than 400 detained at Navalny memorials in Russia: Rights group](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/2/17/more-than-100-detained-at-navalny-memorials-in-russia-rights-group) | Al Jazeera | 2024-02-17 | https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/2/17/more-than-100-detained-at-navalny-memorials-in-russia-rights-group | More than 400 people were detained at Navalny memorials and rallies. That is a retaliatory response to a spontaneous public flare-up, not protection or restraint. | `3B.9`, also `3B.8`, `3B.4` |
| [Russia to curb income of 'foreign agents' and those who leave, lawmaker says](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russia-to-curb-income-of-foreign-agents-and-those-who-leave-lawmaker-says-3707363) | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-11-07 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russia-to-curb-income-of-foreign-agents-and-those-who-leave-lawmaker-says-3707363 | Plans to tighten rules on “foreign agents” and people who criticize Russia after leaving would deepen a fear climate and punish dissent, not suppress violence in a narrowly lawful way. | `3B.9`, also `3B.3`, `3B.4`, `3B.6`, `3B.8` |
| [Russia 2024](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2024 | Freedom House describes manipulation of elections, suppression of opposition, and media control. This is the broader background showing that crisis response in 2024 operated inside an already repressive political environment. | `3B.9`, also `3B.4`, `3B.8` |

**Search gap**
I did not find credible 2024 evidence that Putin used domestic crises to build durable, rights-respecting restraint. The only clear protective action was immediate security tightening after Crocus; the rest of the record points to retaliation, scapegoating, and selective punishment.
